title: Summer Games
build: The PAL G64 of Epyx's disk (directory "SUMMER GAMES"): the boot file SUMMER GAMES and SGLOAD, the engine B unpacked to $0C00-$3EFF, the opening ceremony A, six event files D, E, F, H, I and K each unpacked over $4000 upward (swimming over $1000-$BEFF), the world records WR and DEFAULT, and the unused files L and M; a second PAL image and an NTSC image were supplied too

Pike shapes, then from shape 61 ($8F40) the half-pike (shapes 61-99)

The last layout and standing shapes
The splash, shapes $8D-$92: small, large and medium for each side (left $8D-$8F, right $90-$92), chosen by the entry
The judges' score cards, shapes $93-$9D: "0." to "10." with a gap for the half, then $9E "0" and $9F "5" ORed into the gap
The event starts: sets the interrupt and screen, builds the bit-reversing table, clears every score, then starts with player 0's first dive

Before each dive: resets the stack and the dive's state (state 4, layout position, standing pose $0C, rising speed $ED, X $E7, Y $44), takes the starting difficulty from start_diff for this dive, arms the bonus bits, and puts up the text screen. In practice it offers the dive menu; in competition it says whose dive and which it is
Competition: "GET READY FOR DIVE #" with the player's name, the dive number and "THIS WILL BE A" and the dive's name, then waits for the button
Practice: "CHOOSE TYPE OF DIVE TO PRACTICE:" and the five lines FORWARD, BACKWARD, REVERSE, INWARD and QUIT, with an arrow on the chosen line
Waits up to nine frames for the button; then reads the stick: up moves the arrow up, down moves it down
The button: QUIT goes back to the engine's menu at $0900; any dive goes on

Sets the spin direction from dive_flags bit 0 (backward and reverse spin the other way) and, when bit 1 (which way the diver faces) differs from the last dive, mirrors every shape with $085F set; then shows the picture, colours the diver by player and hands over to the interrupt in state 0
The main program idles here: the dive runs in the raster interrupt
After the seventh judge: the text screen with "JUDGES SCORES:", the seven cards in a row, "DIVE RATING FOR:" and the player's name
"DISCARD HIGH AND LOW TO GET:" and the five middle scores' sum (dive_raw, in half points), then that sum times five into $21/$22

"MULTIPLY BY DIFFICULTY RATING:" and the rating as x.x, then multiplies (mult_difficulty) and prints "TOTAL POINTS:" with the product. The three BCD bytes go into this player's slot for this dive, which is marked scored, and add_total sums the player's four dives
Competition: "CURRENT STANDINGS:", one line per player with the name and the four dives' points, the rows spaced by three, or two with seven or more players
Waits for the button, then the next player; after the last player, the next dive; after the fourth dive, save_results and back to the engine at $0900
State 4 or more: sprites off
State 2 or 3: the splash and the judges

The raster interrupt, line $F7, every frame: blanks the diver's sprites while their buffers change, counts the frame and runs the state: 0 on the platform, 1 in the air, 2 the splash, 3 the judges' cards, 4 and above the text screen with sprites off
State 0: the fire button takes off (state 1); the diver stands until then

State 1, a frame of the dive: the diver drifts left a pixel, and the vertical speed, a signed byte, adds a sixteenth of itself to Y while it rises by one a frame (gravity). At Y $F5 the diver is in the water

The entry: judge_entry scores the pose, then the pose's entry type (entry_type) picks the splash's spread, its two shapes and places, its loudness and how long it lasts, and the noise starts on all three voices

In the air the stick picks the body position (stick_dir: 0 right tuck, 1 left half-pike, 2 down pike, 3 up layout). Each position adds 3 to the difficulty the first time it is used, through its bonus bits

The spin: the position's rate for this dive (spin_rate) adds to an accumulator, and each carry turns the diver one of twelve frames, down for forward spins and up for backward ones. Out of the standing pose ($0C) both start at frame 11
Passing frames 2 and 8, each half-turn, adds 0.4 to the difficulty: the CMP that finds the frame leaves the carry set, so the ADC #$03 adds 4

Draws the diver: keeps the pose and spin accumulator for the scoring, takes the pose from the position's base and the frame (pose_index), and places up to four sprites from the pose's offsets around X and Y, copying their shapes into buffers $39-$3C
Moves the two splash shapes down a row and apart by the spread each frame
Pulls Y, X and A and returns from the interrupt
State 2 goes to the splash

State 3: the judges' cards come up one at a time, each after a random 32-54 frames, or at once once the button has been pressed. Each card is a digit shape for the whole points with the "0" or "5" ORed in for the half. After the seventh, the button goes to the score screen
State 4 and above: all sprites off
State 2: the splash runs for its time; with $28 frames left the noise is gated off. When it ends the buffers are cleared and seven black sprites placed for the judges' cards (state 3)
Moves the splash shapes down a row and apart
Sets the raster interrupt on line $F7 to dv_irq (and the BRK vector with it), and turns the CIA's interrupts off

Sets the text screen's colours and VIC bank 1, then copies the character ROM's second half ($D800-$DBFF, the upper and lower case set) to $5000 with the CPU's view of it switched in, and puts eight drawn characters from frame_chars over its first codes
Switches the I/O back in and goes on to set the sprites up

Clears the sprite buffers ($4E00-$4FFF), points sprites 0-6 at $39-$3F, single colour and unexpanded, sprite 0 white and 1-3 light red until start_dive colours them by player, splash sprites on line $E3, and loads the SID from sid_init
Steps the random number in $1A/$1B and returns a byte of it
Sets the screen position from A (column) and Y (row), then prints message X
Prints message X in its colour from msg_lo/msg_hi/msg_colour, up to the $FF that ends it
Sets the screen position, then falls into print_name; nothing calls this way in
Prints player X's 16-character name from the engine's record at $0800 + 32X
ORs shape A into sprite buffer Y: shape n is at $8000 + 64n
Copies shape A into sprite buffer Y (buf_lo/buf_hi)

Mirrors every diver shape left to right, three bytes a row through bit_reverse with the two side bytes swapped, from $8040 up to $A33F, by rewriting its own addresses for each shape; then negates the pose X offsets, so the diver faces the other way

The picture: waits for line $F1, turns on multicolour bitmap mode ($D018 = $78: screen $5C00, bitmap $6000), black background, and copies the colour RAM from $5800
Clears the text screen and draws its frame: a top border, 23 rows of spaces and a bottom border, then the double line on row 2
Carry set only on the frame the fire button goes down; a held button counts once
The stick's direction in A: 3 up, 2 down, 1 left, 0 right, negative for none

Writes the character in A with the colour in text_colour and moves on

Prints a BCD digit with a leading 0, then a point
Prints a judge's score in half points as " n.0" or " n.5"

At the end of the competition, for each player: prints the total as text into the engine record's result field ($0810 + 32X), then writes its three BCD bytes after it as the score
Adds a player's four dives in BCD into the fifth slot, their total

Scores the entry from the pose and the spin: only the layout scores. Its base (entry_base) is 100 at frames 5 and 11, head or feet straight down, 80 one frame off, 32 two off and 0 flat; the spin accumulator's top nibble, read the way the dive turns, takes or adds the step (entry_step_fwd or entry_step_back) for how far it is to the next frame
Divides the total by five into five judges' scores in half points, the remainder spread one each
Moves a point from one random judge to another, unless the first has none or the second has 20
Adds the high and low judges: one judge's score plus 0 or 1, at most 20, and another's less 0 or 1
Shuffles the seven scores nine times
Turns the 16-bit number in $10/$11 into BCD in $12-$14
Divides $10/$11 by ten: the quotient back in $10/$11, the remainder in A
A times 32
A times 16
Clears the 40 score slots, eight players by five, and marks them all unscored
Multiplies $21/$22 by the difficulty, shifting and adding, then to decimal
